beats.care: More AC buses with CCTV, panic buttons and live tracking. EV owners near these depots also get public charging.
beats.what: Transport Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh opened charging stations at Anand Vihar ISBT and DTC depots in Nand Nagri, Rohini Sector-37, Nangloi and Keshopur.
beats.why: Delhi wants cleaner air and more buses. Its total fleet is about 6,988, including 1,750 CNG buses.

cards.body: The new buses are low-floor and air-conditioned, with CCTV, panic buttons and real-time tracking.
These five are public EV charging stations, opened at a bus terminal and DTC depots.

cards.q: How often do you take DTC buses?
Roughly what share of Delhi's buses are now electric?
cards.why: 5,238 of about 6,988 buses are electric — roughly 75%.

hook: Three in four Delhi buses are now *electric*. What's new?

learn.t: Anand Vihar ISBT handles about 2,300 buses and 1.25 lakh commuters every day.

sources.name: The Statesman
sources.title: Delhi to add 150 electric buses, take zero-emission fleet to 5,238

tldr: Delhi is adding 150 electric buses and opened five public EV charging stations, taking its e-bus fleet to 5,238.
watch: Delhi aims for about 14,000 buses in its fleet by 2028-29; no route dates for the new buses yet.
